title: DHS 'ICE IS NICE' Weekend Enforcement Highlights Criminal Arrests — Administration Strategy of Featuring Worst Cases to Frame Mass Enforcement Campaign
detail: The Department of Homeland Security published its weekly 'ICE IS NICE: Over the Weekend' press release on May 4, 2026, covering enforcement operations conducted over the May 3–4 weekend. The release highlighted the arrest of Farhan Ahmed, a Pakistani national convicted of first-degree manslaughter in Queens, New York, alongside sex offenders, pedophiles, and drug traffickers. The 'ICE IS NICE' series — a weekly DHS communications staple under the Trump second term — is specifically designed to lead with the most extreme criminal alien arrests to build public support for an enforcement apparatus that operates far beyond dangerous individuals. Data from TRAC Reports and the UC Berkeley Deportation Data Project consistently shows that approximately 59% of weekly ICE arrests as of April 2026 involve immigrants with no criminal conviction — a figure directly contradicted by the administration's PR framing. Border Czar Tom Homan and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin counter that all undocumented individuals are priorities for removal regardless of criminal record, reflecting the administration's formal position that unlawful presence itself constitutes a sufficient enforcement basis. The weekend operations were part of ICE's ongoing enforcement campaign averaging 7,369 arrests per week as of late April 2026 — down from the January 2026 peak of ~40,000/month but far above historical levels. DHS has published parallel weekly 'ICE IS NICE' releases since early 2025 as part of a deliberate policy to normalize mass civil immigration enforcement by association with violent criminals. Civil rights advocates have called the framing misleading and argue it contributes to widespread community fear disproportionate to actual enforcement targeting criteria.
